title: Marketplace transaction launch readiness
goal: Complete and certify the marketplace buyer, seller, order, payout, cancellation, refund, and webhook lifecycle

in: Listings, storefronts, carts, checkout, orders, seller onboarding, payouts, cancellation, refunds, webhooks, audit trails, and authorization
out: Advanced music rights and institutional commerce integrations

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The deployed staging listing-to-payout lifecycle passes in Stripe test mode
evidence: STATE not_started means the criterion as written is NOT met: it is a deployed-staging claim with no hosted evidence. It does NOT mean no work was done. The application paths the criterion certifies are locally covered; the hosted run has not happened.
BLOCKED. No staging deployment, no Stripe test-mode credentials, no hosted webhook evidence in this environment. No payment-provider call was made and no Stripe result is claimed.

Local preconditions now in place for whoever runs it: checkout idempotency and no-double-charge, webhook replay takeover, monotonic paid/failed/refunded transitions, cancellation, refund, and buyer-scoped entitlement download are covered by 21 files / 205 vitest tests and 11 jest suites / 52 tests.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Buyer, seller, and tenant authorization denials pass at the server boundary
evidence: STATE not_started means the criterion as written is NOT met, because the tenant third is blocked. It does NOT mean buyer and seller denials are absent; the sub-part breakdown follows.

MET and locally tested — buyer denial. app/api/marketplace/delivery/[orderItemId]/route.ts returns 403 to a non-buyer and its increment is filtered on buyer_user_id; the guest claim route refuses unsettled payments and refuses a claim that loses the buyer_user_id race.

MET and locally tested — seller denial. orders/[id]/refund resolves the actor server-side and returns 403 to a buyer and to a non-participant before any Stripe call; orders/[id]/cancel does the same and then routes a seller to the buyer-only cancellation rule.

MET and locally tested — persona/tenant denial. A verified venue, artist, service, or organization acting persona that owns seller_user_id is denied 403 persona_storefront_schema_not_ready at both money routes, using the same canonical identity contract the listing and storefront launch gates already apply. Previously the persona gate covered the create path but not the money paths.

NOT MET — real tenant-scoped authorization. The order lifecycle is scoped by seller_user_id alone; seller_entity_id and seller_entity_type appear in no active migration, so the persona columns are still MKT-002 schema. Asserted denial is not tenant scoping. This is a blocker, not a claim.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Money mutations and webhooks are idempotent, replay-safe, auditable, and produce safe error states
evidence: STATE not_started means the criterion as written is NOT met, because replay safety is unproven against a real database. It does NOT mean the invariants are unverified locally; the sub-part breakdown follows.

MET locally — checkout idempotency. Keyed on the durable marketplace_checkout_attempts row plus the partial unique index on marketplace_orders.idempotency_key, never on an in-memory or pre-check flag. 8 route tests drive the real path, including the concurrent-first-request 23505 case, which creates zero Stripe sessions.

MET locally — webhook replay safety, fixed this wave. A previously failed event is now taken over and re-processed instead of being answered 200 as a duplicate, so a captured payment can no longer be left permanently unfulfilled. Previously a delivered retry was silently dropped.

MET locally — monotonic transitions. A redelivered paid session cannot resurrect a refunded order; payment_failure cannot downgrade a captured order; a partial refund holds the payout without marking the order refunded; a live attempt with an order still resumes after its window closes.

MET locally — auditable and safe error states. The refund route fails closed with refund_audit_failed when its idempotency ledger write matches no row; the event row persists only last_error='internal_error' with no raw provider payload and no database message; a lost CAS returns 409 rather than a signed URL.

NOT MET — replay safety against a real database. Every assertion runs against an in-memory stand-in for the service-role client. The unique constraints, the RLS posture, and genuine 23505 behaviour are SQL contracts proven by the database lane's DB-011 harness, not by these tests.

RESIDUAL RISK recorded, not fixed. A delivery killed mid-processing leaves a row in processing_status='processing', which the claim does not take over. Reclaiming it safely needs a liveness signal such as processing_started_at, which is a database-lane schema change and outside this working set.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Deferred marketplace variants are gated and cannot bypass the canonical launch flow
evidence: STATE not_started means the criterion as written is NOT met: it is a deployed-flow claim. It does NOT mean the gates are absent; the code-level gating is met and tested.

MET at code level, NOT certified deployed. lib/marketplace/__tests__/launch-gates.test.ts asserts physical, service, and external variants each stay 503 unless their own flag is set, and that enabling one does not enable another. The external-listing feed tests assert an unavailable listing publishes no redirectHref.
OPEN on hosted evidence. A deferred variant could only be proven unbypassable by running the flow on a deployment; no such run exists. No hosted result is claimed.

progress.summary: Record correction: acceptance states normalised to the control-plane enum (not_started for all four, with per-criterion evidence stating exactly which sub-parts are met locally and which are not), the check:service-role-allowlist blocker removed after re-running it to exit 0, and the two local_only_unapplied schema blockers corrected now that marketplace_checkout_attempts and marketplace_external_listings are in the active chain. Removed a now-unreachable seller_required branch from the refund route since the explicit role check above it is authoritative.
completed: lib/marketplace/webhook-processor.ts: a claimWebhookEvent step replaces the bare insert guard. A unique-violation event row previously returned duplicate unconditionally, so when a handler had failed and recorded the row as failed, Stripe's own retry was answered 200 and the captured payment was never fulfilled. A row already recorded as failed is now taken over under a conditional update on processing_status, with attempts incremented, and re-processed; only a processed row is a duplicate. Every downstream handler is already idempotent, so the takeover cannot double-charge or double-fulfil.

app/api/marketplace/checkout/route.ts: the Stripe-init rollback now deletes the claimed marketplace_checkout_attempts row. Previously the row survived with a null order_id, and every retry of that key returned 409 checkout_in_progress for the full 30-minute window even though no money was ever taken and the order had been deleted.

lib/marketplace/checkout-idempotency.ts: resolveCheckoutAttempt is expiry-aware and returns a new reclaim action for a pending attempt that has no order and has passed expires_at. Reclaiming is safe because no order exists to duplicate, the partial unique index on marketplace_orders.idempotency_key still serialises a concurrent winner, and the Stripe session call is keyed by the same client key. A pending attempt that still has an order keeps resuming after its window closes, because resume reuses the same order and the same session and therefore cannot double-charge.

lib/marketplace/order-authorization.ts plus wiring in app/api/marketplace/orders/[id]/cancel/route.ts and app/api/marketplace/orders/[id]/refund/route.ts: a verified venue, artist, service, or organization acting persona that owns seller_user_id is now denied 403 persona_storefront_schema_not_ready at the server boundary, using the same canonical identity contract the listing and storefront launch gates already apply. Before this the persona gate was applied on the create path but not on the money paths, so a persona actor could mutate money on an order whose seller identity the active schema cannot represent.
